notes: Three record shapes, three legacy behaviours (F-0.4/a/b), and all three are contract. Source side is the legacy's archive output per shape, loaded into ow_tp.bronze.p3_audit_legacy_archive with a shape column; target side is ow_tp.silver.audit_archive. For A-estate the legacy produces NOTHING — zero archived rows, no compliance report — and the target must produce nothing too, so the reconciled value is an empty set on both sides and an empty target is the pass, not a gap. For A-tsonly the legacy writes the archive and then exits 1 on a KeyError; the archive contents are still contract, so the rows are compared and the exit code is recorded as a behavioural clause rather than a row. Deletion is not reconciled at all: the legacy deletes nothing on any shape (every delete_item raises on the wrong key schema and is swallowed), and the target never deletes by P3-D04, so both sides report zero source deletions and that agreement is asserted explicitly rather than assumed.

rules: A-estate | A-tsonly | A-full; the shape is part of the key because the same event_id can appear under more than one probe
ISO-canonicalised per the frozen posture; the legacy emits .NET round-trip 'O' format on A-estate records and a plain ISO string on the others
the archived record body, compared as a canonicalised JSON string
0 on every shape on both sides (F-0.4a, P3-D04)
